description:
The floating ball window's own boundary, one permission wide: it may start an operating-system drag of itself, and nothing else about any window.

**Why this is a second capability, and what its narrowing costs now.** It was written when the ball was the only surface that could move. `desktop-pet.json` selects its windows by `pet-*`, which the ball matches — it must, or it would hold no IPC at all — so anything added there is granted to the character windows too, and the sentence that file used to carry (the pet's windows 「may not move any window — including their own」) was true. It is not true any more: the character window has a drag of its own (`DesktopPetRoot.vue` mounts the same gesture on the sprite), and `core:window:allow-start-dragging` is in `desktop-pet.json` for `pet-*`. This file's grant is therefore a **subset** of what the pet's windows already hold rather than a widening of it, and it is kept because the union a window receives is still stated per surface: a reader asking what `pet-ball` may do finds one named window (`pet-ball`, the label `desktop_pet/ball.rs` mints) and one permission, and `command_surface_test.rs` pins both arrays exactly. Collapsing the file into `desktop-pet.json` is a change that also removes those two assertions, and it is not this one.

`core:window:allow-start-dragging` is what `getWindowControls().startDragging()` needs (`platform/window.ts`), and it is the whole of what either surface's drag calls: the compositor owns the movement once it starts, so no position, geometry or monitor permission is granted, and §7.3's ban on per-frame IPC is satisfied by construction rather than by discipline. `snap` — the reference's other half, which parked the window against an edge and persisted the position — is deliberately not wired: it needs `allow-outer-position`, `allow-current-monitor` and `allow-set-position` (three more, for a window that nothing would remember the position of across a launch), and the port declares it optional so its absence is a state the orb states rather than a permission this file can afford.
